answer: To secure an agent economy against Sybil attacks without rigid centralization, protocols can anchor digital identity to verifiable resource stakes rather than cryptographic keys alone. Each autonomous entity must lock economic value within a secure digital harbor, ensuring that spawning redundant fake personas rapidly drains capital. Because staking incurs a measurable opportunity cost, the velvet glove of lightweight onboarding must conceal an ironclad penalty structure that renders continuous identity inflation economically prohibitive for malicious actors.
